paper_title: ChARM Character-based Act-adaptive Reward Modeling for Advanced   Role-Playing Language Agents
caption: The character distribution in RoleplayPref consists of 3 primary categories and 13 subcategories.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The diagram presents a circular representation of character distribution in role-playing contexts, divided into three primary categories: Virtual Characters, Custom Characters, and Real Characters. It contains a total of 13 subcategories, which are visually represented in different sections. The Virtual Characters sector is illustrated in light blue and includes subcategories such as Comic Characters, Movie Characters, Teleplay Characters, Novel Characters, and Game Characters. The Custom Characters section, colored in vivid pink, is smaller and located centrally. The Real Characters sector, shown in green, further breaks down into six subcategories labeled as Scientists, Artists, Athletes, Writers, Musicians, Actors, and Influencers, each displayed in varying shades of green. The diagram lacks specific percentage labels or a legend, and the sectors appear arranged in a circular format without any emphasis on size or arrangement beyond their distribution.
model_annotations.English: The pie chart represents the distribution of characters used in RoleplayPref, categorized into three primary slices: "Virtual Characters," "Custom Characters," and "Real Characters." There are a total of 13 subcategories that fall under these main categories. The "Virtual Characters" slice is colored blue, while "Custom Characters" is highlighted in pink, and "Real Characters" is depicted in green. The subcategories of "Real Characters" include "Scientists," "Artists," "Athletes," "Writers," "Musicians," "Actors," and "Influencers," which are arranged in a clockwise manner from the apex of the green slice. The chart includes labels for all the slices and subcategories, but there are no percentage values displayed within the slices, nor does it appear that any slices are visually emphasized.
model_annotations.German: Das Kreisdiagramm zeigt die Charakterverteilung in RoleplayPref, die in drei Hauptkategorien und 13 Unterkategorien unterteilt ist. Die Hauptkategorien sind "Virtual Characters" in der Mitte, dargestellt in Blau, "Custom Characters" als ein Segment in der Form eines Dreiecks, ebenfalls Blau, und "Real Characters" in Grün. Um die zentrale Gruppe herum sind die weiteren Kategorien angeordnet: "Comic Characters" (hellblau), "Movie Characters" (hellblau), "Teleplay Characters" (hellblau), "Novel Characters" (hellblau), "Game Characters" (hellblau) sowie die Unterkategorien von "Real Characters", die in einem helleren Grün unterteilt sind in "Scientists", "Artists", "Athletes", "Writers", "Musicians", "Actors" und "Influencers". Das Diagramm enthält keine Prozentangaben innerhalb der Segmente und bietet eine Legende, um die Farben den Kategorien zuzuordnen. Die Segmente erscheinen angeordnet, wobei die Hauptkategorien klar hervorgehoben sind.
